Based on the visual evidence and standard Muay Thai training principles (specifically the "Art of Eight Limbs" curriculum often associated with this specific design), here are the likely titles and descriptions for all 8 limbs.

The pattern follows a **Lead/Rear** (or Jab/Cross) logic for each weapon type, where the first number is typically the lead/defensive side and the second is the power/rear side.

### The Full Breakdown

| ID | Limb | Title | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **01** | **FISTS** | **JAB** | Sets range and measures the opponent. |
| **02** | **FISTS** | **MAT** | Lead hand controls distance and sets the trap. *(Visible in screenshot)* |
| **03** | **ELBOWS** | **SLICE** | Cuts through guards and creates openings. |
| **04** | **ELBOWS** | **SMASH** | Devastating close-range power strike. |
| **05** | **KNEES** | **POST** | Controls space and checks forward pressure. |
| **06** | **KNEES** | **SPIKE** | Drives upward to devastate the body or head. |
| **07** | **SHINS** | **CHECK** | Defensive foundation and short-range jamming tool. |
| **08** | **SHINS** | **CUT** | Long-range power that cuts down the opponent's base. |

### Reasoning & Context
*   **The "MAT" (02):** In many modern striking systems (like the one implied here), "MAT" refers to the lead hand's role in "matting down" the opponent's guard or controlling their lead hand to set up the cross.
*   **The Progression:** The terminology moves from **measurement/range** (Jab/Mat) → **close-range destruction** (Slice/Smash) → **structural control/damage** (Post/Spike) → **base elimination** (Check/Cut).
*   **Visual Confirmation:** If you were to click **08 SHINS**, the bottom-right circle on the stick figure would turn red, and the text would update to show **CUT** as the title with a description about using the rear shin to attack the opponent's legs or body.
